translations.answer: Use train.py to train, then run play.py to export a JIT model for deployment. Transfer the policy paths from logs/XBot_ppo/exported/policies to sim2sim.py. When adapting to a new robot, verify the MJCF and URDF joint mapping, and do not only replace file names.
translations.applicability: Applicable to the PPO/JIT export chain in Humanoid-Gym; other export formats require further investigation.
translations.credibility.rationale: The issue has been closed, the environment is clear and there is no conflict. There is formal documentation or an exact citation from an independent replication.

translations.details.attempts.1: Train, then play to export the policy, and finally transfer the model.pt to sim2sim.py.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Verify the version matrix, training commands, export order, and model path against the official README.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: Use the dependency combination and execution order corresponding to the official README.

translations.details.limits.0: The technology stack is outdated; modifications to other robots are still required for asset mapping, joint mapping, default posture, and PD gains.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The command line matches the roboterax/humanoid-gym official README exactly.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Which dependency combination should Humanoid-Gym use to complete the minimal reproduction?
translations.details.problem_statements.1: Why can't sim2sim.py find or load the trained policy correctly?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Sim2sim passing does not mean it can be directly deployed on real hardware; verify action scale, joint order, limits, and emergency stop.
translations.details.suspected_causes.1: The training checkpoint was not exported by play.py or the model path is incorrect.

translations.details.symptoms.1: Missing JIT policy in the simulation when play.py is not run first.
